title: ADMESH: automatic unstructured triangular mesh generator for 2D shallow-water models (Python)

creators.name: Kubatko, Ethan J.
creators.affiliation: Computational Hydrodynamics and Informatics Lab, The Ohio State University

description:
ADMESH 1.0.0 is a Python implementation of the ADMESH library, which generates unstructured triangular meshes for two-dimensional shallow-water models. It ports the 13 stage modules of the 2012 algorithm (Conroy, Kubatko and West, Ocean Dynamics 62, 1503-1517), which build a mesh-size field from boundary curvature, channel width (medial axis), bathymetric gradient and dominant tidal wavelength, then place nodes by distmesh relaxation. A Numba solver replaces the original C MEX file, so installation needs no compiler.

triangulate() accepts a domain object, a TOML or JSON polygon file, an ADCIRC fort.14 file or a registry domain name, and returns a mesh with element quality and boundary segments. The package reads and writes ADCIRC fort.14 and Gmsh 2.2 ASCII files, meshes several domains in parallel with triangulate_batch, and supports an adaptive octree background grid. The optional medial_method argument adds a channel-width size contribution from the 2012 grid method, an octree leaf graph, or the vector distance transform of Kang and Kubatko (2024); it is off by default. Install with pip install admesh2D==1.0.0; the import name is admesh.
